title: load_tasks with a Default
prompt: Write load_tasks(path) that returns the parsed JSON list when the file exists and [] when it does not (use pathlib + json).

tests.name: missing file tolerated
tests.code:
import json as _j, os as _os
if _os.path.exists("tm_probe.json"):
    _os.remove("tm_probe.json")
assert load_tasks("tm_probe.json") == [], "missing file -> []"
_j.dump([{"text": "x", "done": True}], open("tm_probe.json", "w"))
assert load_tasks("tm_probe.json") == [{"text": "x", "done": True}], "existing file is parsed"
_os.remove("tm_probe.json")
assert "Path" in code or "os.path" in code or "exists" in code, "check existence"
tests.hint: from pathlib import Path; if not Path(path).exists(): return []; then json.load.

tests.name: bad json tolerated (stretch)
tests.code:
import os as _os
open("tm_bad.json", "w").write("{not json")
_ok = False
try:
    r = load_tasks("tm_bad.json")
    _ok = r == []
except Exception:
    _ok = True
_os.remove("tm_bad.json")
assert _ok, "corrupt file must either fall back to [] or raise a handled json error"
tests.hint: wrap json.load in try/except and return [] — a strict load is also acceptable.
